title: My Day Timeline
subject: math
learningGoal: Order events in time and read o'clock and half past.
realWorldHook: Clocks help families plan when to wake, eat and go to bed.

materials.item: A clock (analogue if you have one)
materials.householdSubstitution: A drawn clock face or the clock on a phone

noPurchaseRoute: Draw a clock face on paper if you don't have an analogue clock.
parentPreview: Your child puts the events of a day in order and matches a few to o'clock or half-past times.

parent.parentSays: What's the first thing you do every morning?

child.screen: What do you do first every morning?
child.readAloudText: What do you do first every morning?

parent.parentSays: Put these in order: dinner, wake up, school, bedtime.
parent.whyThisWorks: Ordering events is the foundation for understanding time passing.

child.readAloudText: Put your day in order. Drag them from first to last.

parent.parentSays: Show 7 o'clock on the clock. The long hand points to 12.

child.screen: The long hand points to 12. The short hand points to 7. What time is it?
child.readAloudText: The long hand points to twelve. The short hand points to seven. What time is it?

parent.parentSays: Which comes first: lunch or dinner? How do you know?

child.screen: Which comes first, lunch or dinner?
child.readAloudText: Which comes first, lunch or dinner?

parent.parentSays: Ask the two check questions below. Give your child time to think, then note how each one went.
What's your favourite time of day?

child.readAloudText: You made a timeline of your day.

misconceptions.signal: Puts events in a random order or by preference.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: What happened just before you had breakfast?

misconceptions.signal: Reads the long hand as the hour.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: Which hand is shorter? That one tells us the hour.

checkQuestions.parentAsks: Short hand on 3, long hand on 12. What time?

child.screen: Short hand on 3, long hand on 12. What time?
child.readAloudText: Short hand on three. Long hand on twelve. What time is it?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: If the party starts at 4 o'clock and it's 2 o'clock now, how many hours do we wait?

child.screen: Party at 4 o'clock. Now it's 2 o'clock. How many hours to wait?
child.readAloudText: The party is at four o'clock. Now it's two o'clock. How many hours do we wait?

extension: Add half-past times to the timeline.
accessibilityAdaptations: Use a toy clock or turn the hands together.
